mismatch.message: After the player dismisses “The cockatrice bumps into you.--More--”, C prints “You turn to stone...”; JS skips instapetrify() and leaves the prior collision display.

summary: A hurtling cockatrice bumps into the bare-torso Healer. C dothrow.c:mhurtle_step() calls trap.c:instapetrify() after setting the killer, but JS calls note_unported() and skips the stoning message/death sequence. The complete C recording reproduced byte-identically from its independent input recipe.

source.branch: After a monster hurtles into the hero, touch_petrifies(mon->data) and absence of uarmu/uarm/uarmc cause C to set the “being hit by <monster>” killer and call instapetrify(). The call is skipped in JS by note_unported().
callers: For the selected recording, wizard #wiztelekinesis selects the cockatrice and calls mhurtle(mtmp, u.dx, u.dy, 6) in wizcmds.c:wiz_telekinesis(); dothrow.c:mhurtle() then calls walk_path(..., mhurtle_step), which reaches the monster-to-hero collision arm.
dependencies: trap.c:instapetrify is already implemented in js/trap.js; no callee change is needed.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:992-1074 mhurtle_step() performs the collision effects in order. Its u_at(x,y) branch bumps the hero, stops occupation, checks poly hero petrification, then—if touch_petrifies(mon->data) and the hero has no body armor/cloak/shirt—sets killer text, calls instapetrify(), and newsym().
nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:3844-3855 instapetrify() prints the urgent stoning line, sets killer.format/name, and calls done(STONING); js/trap.js already implements this behavior.
js/dothrow.js:735-834 mirrors mhurtle_step() but replaces the source instapetrify call with note_unported("trap.c instapetrify") at the bare-torso monster-to-hero branch.

The admitted v88 case matches through step 66. In segment 0, wizard #wiztelekinesis drives the cockatrice through mhurtle() and walk_path() into mhurtle_step()'s monster-to-hero arm. At step 66, C and JS both show “The cockatrice hisses! The cockatrice bumps into you.--More--”; at step 67 after key space, C shows “You turn to stone...” while JS retains the old collision text and cursor.
